subject: Activation & Funding Pulse — invoice pacing, VAT packets, and holdback triggers
content:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia@acmecorp.com>, Acme Procurement <procure@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Activation & Funding Pulse — invoice pacing, VAT packets, and holdback triggers

Hi Olivia / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for confirming the annual committed credit. To make the activation smooth from an invoicing and VAT perspective, I wanted to propose a clear, short schedule and a minimal list of requested artifacts so we can start issuing invoices and enable drawdown windows when milestones trigger. High level:

- Proposed invoice pacing: 25% at activation, 25% at 90 days, 25% at 180 days, final 25% at 360 days (we can adjust to a monthly phased plan if you prefer).
- Drawdown windows: standard 30-day withdrawal window after each invoice posts; emergency burst requests can be approved by finance (see flow below).
- VAT/evidence: for EU entities we need country VAT registration certificate + proof of business address for invoicing. If Acme provides a consolidated EU VAT cert plus local country evidence, we can mark those invoices as zero-rated where applicable.

Attachments: a sample invoice spreadsheet (invoice_sample_Q3.xlsx) and our activation milestone summary.

Next steps (simple):
1) Olivia / procurement: confirm invoice pacing above or send preferred schedule by EOD Tue.
2) Provide VAT packets for the billing entity (PDFs) or give permission to tax team to validate via TaxServe.
3) We will send a first invoice draft and the DocuSign packet for signature.

If helpful, I can loop in Marcus (payments ops) and Kimberly (billing owner) to agree settlement rails.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0193

Subject: Re: Activation & Funding Pulse — invoice pacing, VAT packets, and holdback triggers

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the clarity. A few notes from our side:

- The activation pacing looks fine but can we move to a monthly 12-step recognition for internal forecasting? That would smooth our cash flows.
- We will provide a consolidated EU VAT cert for Acme Holdings and country-level proof of establishment (attachments coming from our taxops).
- Regarding holdbacks: procurement wants a 5% retention on the activation tranche until SOC 2 evidence is available (expected by end of Q4). Is that acceptable?

I will ask procurement to share the VAT PDFs by Tue EOD.

Olivia Grant

Subject: RE: Fwd: Activation & Funding Pulse — invoice pacing, VAT packets, and holdback triggers

Team — quick operational notes: 

- Monthly invoicing is supported but increases transaction overhead; finance prefers quarterly by default. If Acme requires 12 installments, we'll accept but need to pass the marginal processing cost (nominal). I'll model the fee and share.
- 5% retention: we can invoice at 100% and apply a pending-credit line of 5% that releases once SOC 2 evidence is received. That keeps accounting clean.
- VAT: once we receive the consolidated EU VAT cert and the country proof, billing can flag line items appropriately; TaxServe can validate on our behalf — recommend we copy their validation to the invoice as a note.

Action items for ops: Marcus to confirm ledger tagging for pending-credit. Kimberly to prepare invoice template with retention line and a sample for Acme.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Finance — Redwood Inference
